title: UDP Multicast Streams [docs]
description: added description for UDP Multicast Streams

notes.body: hi @Lekensteyn - I'm a bit confused about this menu item as it's called UDP Multicast Streams in the application, but the template for the docs contains the UDP Multicast Graph. I will fix the title if needed. Other then that - could you please review the description? thank you.

Good catch! I think that "UDP Multicast Streams" is a copy/paste error from the previous option, "TCP Stream Graphs". It should be renamed to "UDP Multicast Streams". Similarly in docbook/wsug_src/WSUG_chapter_use.adoc line 662.

```
|menu:UDP Multicast Streams[]||See <<ChStatUDPMulticastGraphs>>
```

I am not familiar with this functionality, but perhaps the settings below the screen could explicitly be mentioned. Ideally with the effect on the graphs. @geraldcombs do you have an idea who would know best how to describe these settings?
heya! I fixed both title and crossref links for UDP Multicast Streams.

The first sentence is confusing, perhaps OSPF and IGMP are examples of protocol that use UDP Multicast, but it is not clear how this dialog can be used. Some motivation for this feature can be found in the commit message of commit  6b33d50f9054c02be28a846190d279b0a101f744. Could that be used to highlight how this feature can be used?

@JaapKeuter you added support for IPv6 in commit 8e0c81b1d3be984be7487fde5505bf666cb9445e, perhaps you also have some ideas where this feature can become useful?

As the commit message says, this is tailored towards multicast video distribution over the internet. The filter I added was simply for IPv6 multicast Ethernet MAC addresses, besides IPv4 ones, as per https://www.iana.org/assignments/ethernet-numbers/ethernet-numbers.xhtml

+The UDP Multicast Streams window shows statistics for all UDP multicast streams. It includes source addresses and ports, destination addresses and ports, packets counter and other data. You can specify the burst interval, the alarm limits and output speeds. To apply new settings, press btn:[Enter].
+
+With this statistics you can:
+
+* Measure the burst size for a video stream. This uses the sliding window algorithm.
+* Measure of the output buffer size limit, that no packet drop will occur. This uses the Leaky bucket algorithm.
+* Detect the packet loss inside the MPEG2 video stream.
